key_insight: Agent-generated patches can fix the reported compiler bug, but the hard part is matching the broader optimization scope that developers intended.
engineering_relevance: For compiler teams, this suggests AI patching tools are most useful when paired with mechanisms that generalize safely across similar IR patterns, not just the exact failing test.
method: Built a benchmark from real-world LLVM missed-optimization issues.
Compared agent-produced patches against developer patches by optimization scope.
Added historical-knowledge augmentation using retrieval and distillation from prior LLVM optimization pull requests.
evidence_signal: The study reports that agents often optimize the given examples, but many patches only partially overlap with developer intent, while the augmentation techniques improve developer-aligned generalization and show practical benefits on real IR.
watch_item: Broader generalization can help, but it also raises the risk of overapplying an optimization beyond the intended semantics, so validation remains critical.
paper_title: Understanding Agent-Based Patching of Compiler Missed Optimizations
